text.p: Michael Slater opened Australia's tour of India with a brisk unbeaten half-century on the first day of a three-day match against the Indian Board President's XI on Saturday.
Australia reached the close at 122 for one in two hours of play after a wet pitch delayed the start.
Slater, who was dropped when on 29, posted his half-century in 86 deliveries and will resume on Sunday on 52.
He struck medium pacer David Johnson for a six over fine-leg and hit three boundaries.
His opening partner and skipper Mark Taylor, who opted to bat first after winning the toss, edged an outswinger from Doddanarasiah Ganesh to wicketkeeper Saba Karim after scoring 20.
Ricky Ponting struck six boundaries on his way to 45 not out.
The touring side would have lost their second wicket on 84 if Ganesh had not spilled an easy catch from Slater off leg-spinner Narendra Hirwani.
The match, Australia's first of a month-long tour, was delayed after a storm on Thursday blew away the covers, exposing the pitch to torrential rain.
The three-day match is Australia's only tour fixture before a one-off test match against India in New Delhi starting on Thursday.
